newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: South African economic team to help Zaire's Kabila.
newsitem.headline: South African economic team to help Zaire's Kabila.

text.p: South Africa is preparing to send experts including representatives from its central bank to help Laurent Kabila rebuild the shattered economy of former Zaire, officials said on Wednesday.

Pretoria is also keen to see Kabila's newly proclaimed Democratic Republic of Congo become the 13th member of the Southern African Development Community (SADC), which aims to establish a regional common market within eight years.

South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel told businessmen in Zimbabwe's capital that Africa's third largest country badly needed to establish viable monetary and fiscal authorities, and South Africa was willing to help.

"As we sit hear today, Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad is convening a team of people comprising a number of key government institutions and also representatives of our independent Reserve Bank," he said. "They will leave for the Democratic Republic of Congo very soon."
Manuel said it was important for the whole continent that the country should be a success story following the ousting of former president Mobutu Sese Seko.
"We see it as fundamental as part of a wider vision for an African renaissance to put effort into the country now."
Following a seven-month civil war, Kabila on Saturday changed the name of the country to the Democratic Republic of Congo and declared himself president.
Addressing the same meeting, South Africa's President Nelson Mandela reiterated his support for Kabila and said there was no reason to think that one dictatorship would be replaced by another.
"All fears that he (Kabila) might replace one dictatorship with another are baseless," he said.
Mandela criticised unnamed Western governments who had supported "vicious" dictators in the past and were now lecturing Kabila on democracy.
"President Kabila is an outstanding thinker, a dynamic leader, who is committed to peace in that country," Mandela said.
South African Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo said former Zaire could be a candidate for inclusion in SADC.

"Hopefully it will be possible for them to be included in SADC as the 13th country, although that will be up to the SADC summit," he said, adding that the enormous untapped hydroelectric power of the Congo River could be a boon to the whole region.
Analysts say former Zaire has huge economic potential which may at last be unlocked following the change of government.
Hopes centre on the mining industry, once the world's largest copper producer, which has sunk into chronic disrepair but is now attracting interest from international mining houses.
